name: Message stack
what: Chat notifications pop in one after another, creamy glass bubbles with an app icon, a title line and the message; each lands with a soft glow and the newest pushes the older ones up, stacking above the bottom of the frame. Over a video the real footage is frosted under each bubble.
origin: A MotionLab original for a common need (messages from viewers stacking up over a talking head), rebuilt in our HyperFrames way from the look and motion of an MIT-licensed Python effect (claude-video-effects, messages / msg_bubble); 2026-10-27
motion: a message pops in every 14 frames from f4 (closer when there are more than 5: all of them within 56 frames): it rises 26 px and grows from 0.82 (back.out, 9 f), fading in over 4 f, with a soft glow that blooms in 3 f and settles over 19 f; each newer one pushes the older ones up by one bubble and gap (power3.out, 8 f), so the newest sits at the bottom of the stack; older ones pushed past the top fade; in the hold the bubbles drift 2 px out of step and the glow breathes; at the end they sink 30 px and fade (power2.in, 8 f). With the default four messages: pops at f4, f18, f32, f46.
